title: Vessel level control and shutdown
goal: A reader can trace the vessel level regulation loop and the independent high-level inlet shutdown while distinguishing instrument locations, tags, and signal types.

rubric.must: The vessel V-101 outlet is visibly connected through LV-101 to the product tank, and LV-101 is identifiable as an actuated control valve.
The level measurement path connects V-101 to LT-101, then LIC-101, then the LV-101 actuator, with each endpoint identifiable.
LSHH-202 senses V-101 and has a separate signal path to the inlet shutoff valve XV-202 that does not pass through LIC-101 or LV-101.
Solid process piping, dashed electrical signals, pneumatic signals with diagonal marks, and dotted capillary sensing lines are visually distinguishable.
LT-101 and LSHH-202 have plain field instrument bubbles, while LIC-101 has a clearly visible control-room horizontal location mark.
LT-101, LIC-101, and LV-101 are readable as loop 101 tags, while LSHH-202 and XV-202 are readable as separate loop 202 tags beside or inside their own symbols.
FC is legible beside the XV-202 shutoff actuator and FO is legible beside the LV-101 outlet control actuator.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source and the rubric, without seeing the engine's own output. It preferred the svg: The SVG satisfies the required connections, instrument identities, signal styles, and fail positions, while the picture violates multiple blockers and major requirements.
